payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When a record moves under a parent that the type rule allows, the tracker records the move and the record shows the new parent.
- When a record moves under a parent that the type rule refuses, the tracker refuses the move by name and gives the allowed parent types.
- When a record moves to the top level, its type may be one that sits under no record.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When a consumer finds a record under a parent that the record type rule does not allow, I want to move it under another parent or to the top level, so I can bring the ledger in line with the rule without re-creating the record.

## Evidence

handily, 2026-10-14, record handily-fwkt.18: the epics handily-fwkt.2, handily-fwkt.8 and handily-fwkt.9 sit under the epic handily-fwkt, which the rule refuses (record_types.py CHILD_TYPES: an epic sits under no record). tracker undep refuses their edge: a parent-child edge is not retractable, because removing it re-parents the record while its id still spells its parent, so re-parenting needs its own verb. basicly 0.23.1 has no such verb. Today a retype of such a record is refused, and the record stays out of rule.

## Scope

The tracker kit: a re-parent verb, the id rule for a moved record, the type rule check on the new parent, and its tests.
payload.requirements: - A consumer can move a record to a new parent or to the top level, with the type rule checked, and without re-creating the record.
payload.title: tracker: a re-parent verb that moves a record under a new parent
